newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Second Czech GSM mobile phone service set to roll.
newsitem.headline: Second Czech GSM mobile phone service set to roll.

text.p: Radiomobil a.s., partly owned by a consortium led by Germany's DeTeMobil, said on Thursday it aimed to take 50 percent of the Czech GSM digtal mobile phone market just months after next week's launch.

Klaus Tebbe, general director of Radiomobil, told a news conference that his company would start selling its services at 200 dealerships on Monday, covering 30 percent of the 10.4 million Czech population with its signal.

Tebbe said the service called "Paegas" would aim to reach a 50 percent share of new GSM connections in several months, as it seeks to overtake Eurotel s.r.o., which he said had 20,000 GSM clients since it started its service in July.
A spokeswoman for Eurotel, which has been gearing up for a price war with Paegas, declined comment on the number of GSM clients the firm had already signed.
Radiomobil plans to cover 50 percent of the population by the end of this yaer, and 80 percent by April of the next year.
"We have invested over $100 million into our operations in the Czech Republic," Tebbe said, adding that another $100 million would be invested by mid-1997.
The consortium C Mobil -- led by the mobile arm of Deutsche TeleKom AG along with STET SpA of Italy and a few Czech companies holding marginal stakes -- has been leading the rollout of Paegas.
It won a government tender in March to partner with Czech transmission company Ceske Radiokomunikace a.s. to set up the country's second GSM service.
Eurotel s.r.o., which was granted licence under an earlier agreement, is a joint venture of Czech fixed-line operator SPT Telecom a.s., U.S. Bell Atlantic Corp and U.S. West Media Group.
Eurotel, which also operates the country's only analog NMT mobile system, has cut its prices several times since the beginning of the summer as the Paegas launch neared.
"Despite that, we know the their sales have not been so good recently. People are waiting what the competition will bring," Tebbe said.
A Eurotel spokeswoman, Eva Tatounova, denied Radiomobil's claim that sales were slowing ahead of Paegas's launch.

"I don't know where Mr. Tebbe gets his information. We are very surprised by the continuing interest (of clients)," Totounova told Reuters. She said Eurotel's network already covered 70 percent of the Czech population.
Tebbe said he believed that Czech mobile phone penetration could reach 10 percent of the population in the next five years from currently less than one percent.
Radiomobil said in March it expected the firm's operation to gross about 300 million marks per year by 2005 with just over half the Czech mobile telephone market.
